frontPage.headline: Periodic Labour Force Survey to be modified to cover gig workers and unpaid household labor
frontPage.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation is preparing to update the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) framework to measure labour underutilisation, informal gig economy employment, and unpaid household work. The revised survey aims to capture structural shifts in India's labor market and provide better data for socio-economic policymaking.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Crucial for GS III Employment topics and GS II Welfare policies. Capturing gig work and unpaid care labor directly addresses data gaps in GDP estimation, female labor force participation rate (FLFPR), and social security planning.

frontPage.headline: RBI Bulletin highlights broad-based food inflation and domestic demand resilience amidst global volatility
frontPage.summary: The Reserve Bank of India’s latest bulletin highlights that consumer price index (CPI) inflation has edged up due to generalised food price increases, with rural areas experiencing higher price pressures than urban centers. However, strong domestic consumption demand continues to anchor India's overall economic growth momentum despite external trade headwinds.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Directly impacts GS III Inflation and Monetary Policy. Highlights the persistent threat of food price shocks on headline inflation and rural purchasing power.

frontPage.headline: UN Loss and Damage Fund operationalised with $20 million climate relief payout to Nepal
frontPage.summary: The United Nations Loss and Damage Fund, established during COP27, has earmarked its first-ever country-specific payout of $20 million to Nepal to assist recovery from severe flood disasters. While historic, the payout covers only a tiny fraction of Nepal's estimated $5 billion loss, drawing attention to funding gaps in international climate financing.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Essential for GS III Climate Negotiations and International Environmental Governance. Demonstrates the operationalization phase of the UN Loss and Damage Fund and underscores equity challenges between developing and developed nations.

frontPage.headline: Centre strictly prohibits the re-use and recycling of single-use medical disposables across hospitals
frontPage.summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under the Union Health Ministry has issued directions strictly prohibiting the re-use or recycling of single-use medical devices in all healthcare facilities. The directive addresses severe risks of cross-contamination, hospital-acquired infections, and illegal reprocessing of critical medical consumables.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Relevant for GS II Health Governance and GS III Bio-medical Waste Management. Highlights regulatory enforcement in patient safety and clinical standards.

frontPage.headline: IMD study reveals 70-year climate shift with drier Northwest and wetter Southern India
frontPage.summary: A comprehensive 70-year precipitation analysis by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) shows that Northwest India has progressively turned drier with expanding semi-arid zones, whereas Southern Peninsular India has experienced increased rainfall. The long-term trend highlights changing atmospheric circulation patterns across the subcontinent.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Directly links GS I Physical Geography (Monsoon dynamics) and GS III Agriculture. Demands shifts in cropping patterns, irrigation planning, and regional climate adaptation strategies.

frontPage.headline: Theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen awarded the prestigious Oskar Klein Medal for string theory contributions
frontPage.summary: Renowned Indian theoretical physicist Ashoke Sen has become the first Indian scientist to be awarded the Oskar Klein Medal by Stockholm University. He was recognized for his groundbreaking work on S-duality, black hole entropy, and string field theory.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Important for Prelims scientific awards and recognition of Indian contributions to fundamental physics.

gs1.headline: Mass migration of Blue Tiger butterflies towards Western Ghats begins with North-East monsoon
gs1.summary: Millions of Blue Tiger and Dark Blue Tiger butterflies have started their annual migration from the Eastern Ghats and plains toward the Western Ghats following the onset of the North-East monsoon. This ecological event serves as a crucial indicator of seasonal weather transitions in Peninsular India.
gs1.whyItMatters: Relevant for GS I Geography (monsoonal transitions) and GS III Biodiversity. Illustrates seasonal species movement across distinct ecological corridors in Southern India.

gs2.headline: Parliamentary committee proposes reviewing MPLADS guidelines and funding allocation
gs2.summary: A Parliamentary Standing Committee has chosen to examine the operation of the Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS). The panel will review asset creation guidelines, fund utilization efficiency, and assess proposals for enhancing annual financial allocations to MPs.
gs2.whyItMatters: Directly connected to GS II Parliament and Decentralisation. Raises questions regarding executive implementation by legislative representatives, separation of powers, and audit mechanisms.

gs2.headline: Parliamentary panel recommends intercensal demographic surveys and revised census town criteria
gs2.summary: A parliamentary committee has recommended conducting periodic intercensal sample surveys to bridge critical socio-economic data gaps between decennial censuses. It also urged revising definition norms for 'Census Towns' to make workforce gender criteria more inclusive.
gs2.whyItMatters: Pertains to GS II Governance and policy formulation. Reliable demographic data is foundational for targeted welfare schemes and urban planning.

gs3.headline: Commerce Ministry initiates plans to identify AI-resilient employment sectors in India
gs3.summary: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry is mapping Indian industries and professions that are resistant to automation from generative AI. The strategy aims to position India in high-value, AI-augmented services while safeguarding mass employment across traditional human-centric labor sectors.
gs3.whyItMatters: Relevant to GS III Industrial Policy and Science & Technology. Addresses the economic disruptions caused by rapid AI adoption on IT services and service exports.

gs3.headline: Net Foreign Direct Investment into India turns positive for third consecutive month in September
gs3.summary: India registered a net Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflow of $3.3 billion in September 2026, staying positive for the third straight month. The recovery comes after period of capital repatriation and disinvestments that previously dragged down net capital accounts despite robust gross inflows.
gs3.whyItMatters: Pertains to GS III External Sector dynamics and Balance of Payments.

gs3.headline: RBI Governor reiterates strict listing compliance for Upper-Layer Non-Banking Financial Companies
gs3.summary: The Reserve Bank of India reiterated that Non-Banking Financial Companies classified under the 'Upper Layer' (NBFC-UL) scale-based regulatory framework must mandatorily list on public stock exchanges within three years of identification. The central bank emphasized that regulatory deadlines apply uniformly without special exemptions.
gs3.whyItMatters: Crucial for GS III Financial Sector Regulation. Reflects RBI's tightening oversight over systemically important financial entities to mitigate shadow banking risks.

quiz.question:
Regarding the UN Loss and Damage Fund, consider the following statements:
1. It was formally established during the COP27 UN Climate Conference.
2. The fund is designed specifically to support mitigation projects like solar power plants in high-income countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
quiz.explanation: Statement 1 is correct (established at COP27). Statement 2 is incorrect because the fund specifically provides financial assistance to vulnerable developing nations suffering from climate-induced loss and damage, rather than funding mitigation in high-income nations.

quiz.question:
With reference to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) in India, consider the following statements:
1. It is conducted annually by the Reserve Bank of India.
2. Proposed updates aim to track labour underutilisation, gig workers, and unpaid household work.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
quiz.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect as PLFS is conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under MoSPI, not the RBI. Statement 2 is correct as the government is updating the methodology to capture gig economy and unpaid care work.

quiz.question: The 'Upper Layer' (NBFC-UL) classification framework was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India to regulate:
options: Small microfinance institutions with assets under ₹100 crore
Systemically important Non-Banking Financial Companies based on scale, activity, and risk perception
Only foreign institutional investors operating in IFSC Gift City
Regional Rural Banks operating across multiple state jurisdictions
quiz.explanation: The RBI introduced a Scale-Based Regulation (SBR) framework for NBFCs with four layers (Base, Middle, Upper, Top). Upper Layer consists of systemically important NBFCs subjected to enhanced bank-like regulatory standards, including mandatory listing.

schemes.name: Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
schemes.objective: Enables MPs to recommend developmental works of a durable nature based on locally felt needs in their respective constituencies.
keyFeatures: Fully funded central sector scheme providing ₹5 crore annually per MP in two installments.
Focuses on creating durable community assets such as drinking water, education, public health, and roads.
Requires dedicated percentage allocation for areas inhabited by SC (15%) and ST (7.5%) populations.
schemes.upscRelevance: GS II Scheme implementation, parliamentary oversight, and local asset creation.
